correctness.rationale: For residual sum \(R\) with support radius \(r\), the condition \(t<a_1-r\) makes the conditional central interval lie wholly inside the dominant uniform support, giving the exact identity \(\Pr\{|a_1U_1+R|>t\}=1-t/a_1\). A uniform coupling to \(U_1\) localizes every global maximizer near the unique one-uniform threshold \(t_0\) from arXiv:2305.06235 when \(r\) is small, so the exact plateau identity applies at the optimizer. Differentiation gives \(a_1=t+h(t)\), where \(h(t)=\overline\Phi(\sqrt3 t)/(\sqrt3\,\phi(\sqrt3 t))\), and \(h'(t)=3t h(t)-1\), hence \((t+h(t))'=3t h(t)>0\). The implicit-function and envelope derivatives yield \(t_a=t_0-\varepsilon^2/[6t_0(1-t_0)]+O(\varepsilon^4)\) and \(K(a)=C_*- [t_0/(2Q(t_0))]\varepsilon^2+O(\varepsilon^4)\). The packaged finite-convolution checker reproduces the constants and stress-checks representative small residual vectors; computations are verification, not proof.

value.rationale: The global sharp theorem identifies a one-sparse equality geometry but does not quantify near-equality. The present result answers the natural stability question with an exact dimension-free second-order law, identifies the tangent-space quadratic coefficient, and shows that all residual-coordinate details disappear locally except through their total squared mass. This is a structural refinement of a sharp probability inequality rather than a routine numerical perturbation.
